title: NSIC Rc 394 (Tubigan 32) Rice Variety: Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaTitle: NSIC Rc 394 Rice Variety: Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaDescription: NSIC Rc 394 (Tubigan 32) is an inbred rice for irrigated lowland, approved in 2015. See its pest and disease ratings, grain quality and where it grows best.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 394 is an inbred rice variety for irrigated lowland, known locally as Tubigan 32. The NSIC approved it in 2015. PhilRice bred it. Its days to harvest and trial yield are not published yet, but its pest ratings and grain quality are below.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 394, or Rc 394, this is the one. Compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

This variety's days to harvest and trial yields are not published yet. So ask the seed seller or your municipal agriculturist for the figures from the trials in your region before you plan the season. Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it. blocks.text: So scout early for [rice blast](/diseases/rice-blast), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With intermediate amylose, expect rice that is soft but not sticky. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it wet direct seeded. It was tested and found suitable in Calabarzon. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 394?
items.a: It is known as Tubigan 32. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.
The NSIC approved it in 2015. PhilRice bred it. Its days to harvest and trial yield are not published yet, so ask for the regional trial figures before you plant.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In trials it was weak against rice blast, tungro, sheath blight. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
It has intermediate amylose, 19.9 percent. So it cooks soft but not sticky.
